summary: Spec bug: the harness's own arithmetic overflows. The implementation's cups are all proven exactly as in isqrt.wat; only the harness False cup fails, and a run refutes it at n = 2³²−1.

cups.why: unfold $sq_le: 0·0 = 0 ≤ ext_u(n). [R5a] fed automatically (no prove line): the goal holds with no hypothesis.

cups.goal: $is_isqrt(ext_u(#r), ext_u($n)) at the taken edge (#r = loop-head φ)

hyps.origin: refined local re-entered at loop head (R8)

cups.why: intervals pin u(r) = 65535 (§3.3), so r² and (r+1)² = 2³² are constants; ext_u(n) < 2³²; invariant gives r² ≤ n. [R5a] fed automatically (no prove line): from the facts of lines 30, 34.

hyps.origin: br_if taken edge (gt_u normalized to lt_u)

cups.why: unfold $is_isqrt: the sq_le case is the invariant; the other conjunct is the edge fact, the same terms by value numbering. [R5a] fed automatically (no prove line): from the facts of lines 30, 47.
u(r) ≤ 65534, so i32.add does not wrap (q = 0 by intervals) and r+1 ≤ 65535. [R5a] fed automatically (no prove line): from the fact of line 34.

no wrap in i32.add (r ≤ 65534) nor in either i64 product (≤ 65535² < 2⁶⁴), so both sides expand to r² + 2r + 1 over the same monomial r². [R5a] fed automatically (no prove line): from the fact of line 47.
R22: after `br $grow` the rest is dead; the fall-through edge into `end` is fed by False.
both edges bind $r to the loop-head φ, so the join keeps #r; the virtual slot ext_u(#r) is the same id in both atoms.

prove_error.text: not implied by [¬$is_isqrt32(#q,$n) @82, $is_isqrt(ext_u(#q),ext_u($n)) @79]: the i32 product (r+1)·(r+1) may wrap (its wrap variable stays in the problem); countermodel r = 65535, n = 4294967295

cups.why: the code is right and proven; the spec is wrong. $is_isqrt32 computes (r+1)² in i32, which is 2³² ≡ 0 at r = 65535, so for n ≥ 65535² = 4294836225 (unsigned) the check says 'n < 0' and fails. The fix is harness discipline §6.3: compute the check in i64.
cups.strict_error: reachable: needs False; nothing feeds it (could not decide (inexact step on wrap(mul($isqrt($n), $isqrt($n)))); add a lemma)
